image_description: A group of approximately thirteen adults standing on a grassy lawn in front of a stone building with Gothic-style arched windows. Most individuals are wearing black academic gowns with colored facings (pink, red, yellow) and hoods. Several hold rolled red diplomas. One individual on the far right wears a more elaborate red and yellow ceremonial robe. A person in casual clothing is visible in the background on the left.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The garments clearly drape from the shoulders down, covering the torso and legs, creating the expected rectangular silhouette typical of academic regalia.
The gowns exhibit bilateral symmetry and feature a distinct vertical opening down the center front, revealing the attire underneath.
The fabric hangs loosely and voluminously, effectively hiding the specific body shapes of the wearers, consistent with the definition.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wide open sleeves extending well below hand level.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The sleeves are visibly wide and bell-shaped, hanging significantly lower than the wrists/hands of the subjects, a key identifier for this class.
The front edges of the gowns form distinct panels that frame the center opening, often accented with colored velvet or fabric facings.
Subjects are visibly wearing suits, ties, and formal dresses underneath the open gowns.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Heavy matte fabric typically black polyester or wool blend.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fabric appears opaque, heavy, and non-reflective (matte), consistent with traditional gown materials like polyester or wool blends.
There is no significant specular highlight or sheen on the black fabric; it absorbs light smoothly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Characteristic sleeve drape extending past the wrist.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The drape of the sleeves is pronounced and extends well beyond the wrist area, matching the taxonomic description.
